thread.title: SunZia Wind Project set to become largest U.S. wind farm in New Mexico
thread.title_full: SunZia Wind Project set to become largest U.S. wind farm in New Mexico

author: beaver state news
title: SunZia Wind Project set to become largest U.S. wind farm in New Mexico
text:
The SunZia Wind Project in central New Mexico is expected to begin commercial operations this month, bringing 916 turbines online and establishing itself as the nation’s largest wind farm, according to a Jun. 17 report.
The project will provide 3,650 megawatts of summer capacity, surpassing the combined capacity of the next two largest U.S. wind farms. Pattern Energy began construction three years ago after nearly two decades of planning and permitting. With its significant output, SunZia will almost double New Mexico’s total wind capacity.
Spanning three counties, the northern section across San Miguel and Lincoln counties includes 242 turbines, while the southern portion across Lincoln and Torrance counties has 674 turbines. Some turbines were already supplying electricity to the grid during testing phases by April 2026. The facility is now connected to a new 550-mile transmission line designed to deliver power from New Mexico into Arizona and Southern California.
The introduction of such large-scale wind power aims to supply homes, businesses, and cities with electricity without heavy reliance on fossil fuels, contributing to cleaner air and greater grid stability. The increased availability of renewable energy also helps utilities diversify their sources and reduce vulnerability to fluctuations in fuel prices driven by international events.
Energy experts say that at its scale of 3,650 megawatts, SunZia stands apart from other operating U.S. wind projects and is rapidly changing New Mexico’s clean energy landscape by making wind power the state’s leading source of generation.
